chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about at what amount the thief's hand is cut off. He said: The minimum is one-third of a dinar.

key_terms.دِينَارٍ: dinar (a gold coin used as a unit of currency)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for hadd punishment of cutting the hand in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Samaanah reports that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defined the minimum threshold for *hadd* amputation as one-third of a dinar, establishing a precise monetary baseline for theft. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking the severity of the punishment to the intrinsic value of the stolen goods, ensuring proportionality in judicial application. The specification of 'one-third' highlights the rigorous attention to detail in fiqh derived from the Imams regarding the conditions of *qat' al-yad*.
